name: United Arab Emirates

findings.summary: Khazna, a G42 company, is building a 1GW Stargate UAE cluster inside the 5GW UAE-US AI Campus in Abu Dhabi; first 200MW under construction, targeted for 2026. Partners: OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, Cisco, SoftBank.
findings.analyst_inference: Facility controller is domestic (G42/Khazna) but the tenant (OpenAI) and the accelerators are US, and US export-licence conditions give Washington leverage over use. Epoch AI (Jul 2026) still listed 0 MW operational; whether the 200MW phase is live by Oct 2026 is unconfirmed.

findings.summary: First OpenAI for Countries partnership: alongside the Stargate UAE cluster, OpenAI says the UAE will be the first country to enable ChatGPT nationwide, across education, health, energy and government services.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 1: announced partnership with no published contract terms or value. Gulf News notes claims of free ChatGPT Plus for all residents were not confirmed.

findings.summary: US Commerce granted Microsoft a first-of-its-kind licence to ship Nvidia GB300 GPUs (tens of thousands) to the UAE; reported November 2025 alongside Microsoft's UAE commitment of about $15.2bn through 2030.
findings.analyst_inference: The $15.2bn figure is Microsoft's total UAE commitment (incl. $1.5bn G42 equity), not the chip value, so announced_value_usd is left null. Separate from the Nov 2025 G42 authorisation already in us_chip_export_posture.json.

findings.reversal_of: Huawei and other Chinese equipment in G42's systems
findings.summary: As a condition of Microsoft's $1.5bn minority investment in G42 (April 2024), G42 agreed to divest from China and, per New York Times reporting relayed here, strip Huawei and other Chinese equipment from its systems.
findings.analyst_inference: Layer and tier of the reversed equipment are not stated; coded facilities/tier 3 conservatively. Extent and completion of the removal are not independently verified.

findings.summary: Etisalat named Huawei to supply an end-to-end 5G network in the UAE: radio access, service-based 5G core and 5G-ready transport, for deployment in 2019.
findings.analyst_inference: Agreement value and whether Huawei remains sole RAN/core supplier for e& are not shown; likely operational at scale but not evidenced here, so kept at tier 3.

findings.summary: At MWC 2024, e& UAE signed an MoU with Huawei on 5G-Advanced and 50G PON to deliver a '10 Giga' experience (up to 10 Gbps mobile).
Huawei signed a long-term collaboration agreement with Dubai Police to develop a Safe City Innovation Centre; demonstrated facial recognition, video analytics and anti-drone tools at GITEX 2016.

BuzzFeed News reported Hikvision had supplied Dubai with thousands of CCTV cameras, and Huawei showed its FusionInsight footage-search platform at a Dubai government AI conference. No confirmed contract for the Oyoon programme.
findings.analyst_inference: Article undated (internal references suggest 2019). Camera supply implies deployed hardware but no contract, value or date is evidenced, so tier 3 low. Audit 2026-10-22: Huawei only exhibited at a government conference (it was IBM that sought police sales); article dated about May 2019.

findings.summary: MBZUAI released K2 Think V2, an open-source reasoning model published with training data and code, framed as a UAE sovereign model; trained on fewer than 2,000 Nvidia chips.
findings.analyst_inference: Instrument ladder fits a model release poorly; coded tier 2 because government or at-scale adoption is not evidenced. Training compute is US silicon. TII Falcon models not separately coded this pass.

power.null_reason: search budget spent on higher-priority layers; no AI-specific power evidence surfaced (Stargate UAE campus power supply not examined)

corrections.note: Migrated to spec v0.2 (scale, reversal_reason, still_current, builder/financier, base model, opened flags; corroboration recomputed on opened sources) and audit corrections applied.
